sentences.ar: أَتُحَاجُّونِّي فِي اللَّهِ وَقَدْ هَدَانِي وَلَا أَخَافُ مَا تُشْرِكُونَ بِهِ
sentences.en: How can you argue with me about God when He has guided me? I do not fear anything you associate with Him.

parts.label: a
parts.ask: For each clause, decide if it is حال; if it is, tick the ruling for the واو حالية.

parts.label: b
parts.ask: Explain why you chose what you chose.
parts.answer:
First one is haal because when "You" are arguing with me, the state "I" am in is that "Allah has guided me". And since the first one is فعل ماضي with a dhameer raabit, the "Yaa" in 'Hadanee', it is persimmable for it to have a waaw haaliyah.
As for the second part, that also comes under the haaliyyah sentence. Since it is a فعل مضارع منفي with لا, it cannot take a waaw haaliyah, therefore the waaw before it is atifa making it معطوف to the haal before it. It is NOT an independent haal.

sentences.ar: كان زيدٌ يجلسُ على الأرضِ ويُكمل واجباتِه
sentences.en: Zaid used to sit on the floor and complete his assignments.

parts.label: a
parts.ask: For each clause, decide if it is حال; if it is, tick the ruling for the واو حالية.

parts.label: b
parts.ask: Explain why you chose what you chose.
parts.answer: It is not a haal because the jumla is a فعل مضارع مثبت without قد so a waaw haaliyyah is not permissible. Rather, the waaw is atifa and the jumla is ataf to يجلس.

sentences.ar: رَبِّ أَنَّى يَكُونُ لِي غُلَامٌ وَقَدْ بَلَغَنِيَ الْكِبَرُ وَامْرَأَتِي عَاقِرٌ
sentences.en: My Lord, how can I have a son when I am so old and my wife is barren?

parts.label: a
parts.ask: For each clause, decide if it is حال; if it is, tick the ruling for the واو حالية.

parts.label: b
parts.ask: Explain why you chose what you chose.
parts.answer:
First is a فعل ماضي with a raabit so it is optional for it to take a waaw haaliyyah.
Second one is a jumlah ismiyah that does not begin with its dhameer raabit (which is the يـ in this case) so it is also optional for it to take a waaw haaliyyah.
